uncited: Asynchronous Chunk Generation Scheduling controls the rate at which pending voxel chunks are processed from a queue to prevent frame-rate drops during world generation.
It solves the problem of synchronous mesh generation blocking the main thread by limiting the number of chunks generated per frame.

It differs from its parent [Asynchronous Chunk Loading](4216-asynchronous-chynchronous-chunk-loading.md), which offloads work to a thread pool, by performing the generation logic directly on the calling thread (typically the main thread) but throttling the iteration count.

It differs from siblings [Dependency Queue Gating](11597-dependency-queue-gating.md) and [Web Worker Pool for Meshing](14649-web-worker-pool-for-meshing.md) by using a simple percentage-based cap rather than dependency resolution or separate worker threads.
The method processes a list of pending chunk positions, validating regions and generating voxel data or retrieving saved data.
It supports both synchronous (all-at-once) and asynchronous (throttled) modes.
- Output: Updated `pendingChunks` list (processed items removed), generated chunk meshes/voxels added to the scene graph or data store.

- **Time Complexity:** $O(k)$ per frame, where $k$ is the number of chunks processed per frame. $k$ is either $N$ (all pending) or $\lceil 0.1 N \rceil$ (throttled), where $N$ is the total pending chunks.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(1)$ additional memory for the scheduling logic, excluding the memory required for the generated chunk meshes themselves.
- **Limitations:** Still runs on the main thread, so heavy generation can cause stutter if the per-frame cost of a single chunk is high.
Does not handle dependencies between chunks (unlike Dependency Queue Gating).
- **When to use:** When main-thread generation is acceptable but needs rate-limiting to maintain responsiveness.

- **When not to use:** When generation is too heavy for the main thread (use Asynchronous Chunk Loading or Web Worker Pool) or when chunks depend on neighbors being generated first (use Dependency Queue Gating).
It represents a pragmatic approach to managing world generation load in real-time applications where full asynchronous offloading is not required or feasible.
